mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the constraint that no two AuditEntries share the same operation. The injection forces two distinct AuditEntries to reference the same AccessOperation, which is a direct model of an audit-log mutation (an entry being 'overwritten'). Both AppendOnly and FR_010_AuditImmutability check this injectivity and will find a counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj ae1, ae2: AuditEntry | ae1.operation = ae2.operation }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the requirement that every RecordsLookup AccessOperation has exactly one AuditEntry. The injection forces a RecordsLookup operation to exist that has no corresponding AuditEntry atom pointing to it, directly violating SC-001 and SC-002.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenesViolation { some op: AccessOperation | op.opKind = RecordsLookup and (no ae: AuditEntry | ae.operation = op) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the permission matrix fact allows Alloy to populate PermMatrix.Allowed arbitrarily. The injection grants a clinical role access to AuditSearch, which is the most dangerous cross-role escalation (a Doctor reading the IG audit log). LeastPrivilege and FR_011_AuditReadableByIGOnly both depend on the matrix being exactly as specified.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermissionMatrixViolation { Doctor -> AuditSearch in PermMatrix.Allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact lets Alloy assign any ExternalResponse to any operation outcome. The injection creates a Denied operation that returns RecordResponse instead of NotFoundResponse, directly violating SC-003's byte-equivalence requirement and leaking the existence of a patient to a non-care-team clinician.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_ByteEquivViolation { some op: AccessOperation | op.outcome = Denied and op.externalResp = RecordResponse }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the care-team gate fact removes the iff constraint between Permitted outcome and active membership. The injection creates a Permitted RecordsLookup operation for a clinician-patient pair that has no active CareTeamMembership row, directly modelling break-glass access that v1 explicitly prohibits (SC-010).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CareTeamGateViolation { some op: AccessOperation | op.opKind = RecordsLookup and op.outcome = Permitted and (no m: CareTeamMembership | m.clinician = op.caller and m.patient = op.targetPatient and m.status = Active) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact lets AuditEntry fields diverge from the AccessOperation they record. The injection creates an AuditEntry whose clinician field differs from the caller of its linked operation, modelling a misattribution bug (wrong clinician on an audit record) that violates FR-009 and the snapshot-correctness requirement.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionViolation { some ae: AuditEntry | some disj u1, u2: User | ae.clinician = u1 and ae.operation.caller = u2 }
